dataset.purpose: Synthetic long-term banking history for the KBC Time Machine prototype.
dataset.privacy: No real person; all names and profiles are fictional.

methodology.expense_reference: Statbel Household Budget Survey 2024 (category mix); amounts are synthetic.
methodology.income_reference: Statbel reports an average gross monthly salary of EUR 4,076 for full-time employees in 2022; the incomes below are synthetic.
methodology.indexation: Amounts are 2026 levels; 2024 and 2025 are scaled by 0.95 and 0.975 for indexed income and variable spending.

conventions.amount_sign: Negative = money leaves the account, positive = money enters it.

transaction_types.expense: Spending. On the credit card account for card purchases.
transaction_types.refund: Money returned for an earlier expense; nets against its category.
transaction_types.internal_transfer: Movement between the customer's own accounts (two legs sharing transfer_id). Not income, not spending.

conventions.credit_card: Card purchases are recorded on the card account; the full statement is repaid on the 5th of the next month via an internal_transfer (category credit_card_repayment). Count purchases once, never the repayment.
conventions.monthly_summary: income_eur and spending_eur exclude internal transfers; spending is net of refunds.

profiles.name: Jean Lambert
profiles.story: Stable pensioner. His car loan ends in February 2026 and he redirects the freed-up money to savings: monthly transfer goes from EUR 200 to 300 (Mar-Apr 2026) and then EUR 450 (from May 2026). Demo journey: sustained saving increase -> goal.

profiles.name: Sophie & Thomas De Smet
profiles.story: Two incomes, homeowners with a mortgage, uses a credit card repaid in full every month. Holiday pay in May and a 13th month in December fund the summer holiday and Christmas. In September 2026 grocery spending jumps to ~EUR 1,420 (usual ~EUR 900-1,000) on top of back-to-school costs. Demo journey: grocery spike -> cash-flow scenario.

profiles.name: Lucas Peeters
profiles.story: Student living in a kot. Irregular income: parental support, a variable student job (bigger in summer) and a yearly scholarship lump sum. Saves summer earnings and draws on savings during the academic year.
